subject: Discovery follow-up: JSON schema & reliability approach for integration
messages:
From: Sophie Lane <sophie.lane@medixhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@medixhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up + integration questions after today's demo

Hi Hannah —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Raj and I had a couple of technical questions we wanted to lock down before the architecture workshop next week: 

1) Structured output: can you share an example JSON schema you recommend for our discharge-summary generator? We need deterministic fields (diagnosis codes, medication list, followup days) and some free-text notes. We heard about "constrained decoding" — how does Redwood enforce schema validity and what happens when the model still emits malformed JSON?

2) Retry & validation pattern: if the first generation fails schema validation is the recommended approach to re-prompt, or is there an engine-level retry/fallback you recommend? If so, what are typical configs (temperature / decoding method) you see work?

3) SDK & auth: what's the recommended SDK flow for server-side generation vs client-side embeddings calls? Do you support mTLS or short-lived tokens for private deployments?

4) Embeddings + reranker: for our search -> rerank pipeline, what's the typical hybrid approach? Should we do a vector DB top-k followed by a model-based rerank? Any latency/cost expectations?

Appreciate if you can send a short technical note and an example schema before the workshop. I attached the draft MAP for timeline/reference.

—Sophie
Medix Health

Hi Sophie / Raj —

Thanks for the clear list — good timing. I captured this quick recap and attached a first-pass JSON contract (redwood_json_contract_v1.yaml) so your engineers have something concrete to review ahead of the workshop. High-level answers up front, details below from Connor (looping him in).

Summary / next steps:
- We recommend a strict JSON contract for deterministic fields + a free_text block for clinician notes. See attached contract.
- Our recommended reliability approach is: validate -> if invalid, deterministic re-decode with constrained tokens (no sampling) -> if still invalid, fall back to a smaller schema-only extractor or enqueue for human review depending on SLA.
- For SDK/auth: server-side generation with API keys or short-lived tokens is typical; for on-prem we support mutual TLS and integration with customer KMS. Connor included specifics.
- Embeddings + reranker: standard is vector DB top-k (k=50) + model-based rerank over top-k, with a configurable similarity threshold to avoid unnecessary reranks. Expect higher cost but much better precision for clinical signals.

Action items:
1) Connor: please add the detailed decode/validation pattern + suggest exact decoding params we should pilot.
2) Hannah: schedule 60-min architecture deep-dive (invite sent) — target Wed 3/17 10am PT.
3) Sophie/Raj: please review the attached contract and flag any required fields or regulatory constraints.

I'll see you Wed — thanks,
Hannah
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference

From: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Sophie Lane <sophie.lane@medixhealth.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@medixhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + integration questions after today's demo — technical details

Hi all — adding targeted technical guidance. Long but concrete so your engs can validate quickly.

1) JSON contract (reference)- We suggest a strict top-level object with field-level types and enumerations for deterministic items. Example (conceptual):
  {
    "patient_id": "string",
    "discharge_date": "date",
    "diagnoses": [{"code": "ICD10", "primary": "boolean"}],
    "medications": [{"name": "string","dose": "string","route": "string"}],
    "followup_days": "integer",
    "free_text_summary": "string"
  }

  Our contract (attached YAML) includes explicit allowed enums for route and conservative length limits to make decoding easier. Keep the deterministic items near the start of the sequence so prefix caching helps.

2) Constrained decoding + validation strategy- Options we support and recommend for reliability: 
  a) Constrained token sets / grammar: apply token-level constraints while decoding for the deterministic fields (e.g., restrict tokens to digits and dash for dates, or to a small vocabulary for ICD codes) when the model is in deterministic mode. Works well when the schema is regular and the model is large enough to respect constraints.
  b) Function-calling / structured API: if you can refactor to the function-calling flow (model returns a typed response), it reduces malformed output significantly because the runtime enforces the return shape.
  c) Post-generation validation: always run a strict validator (your backend) against the schema. If invalid, do a two-stage retry:
     - Retry #1: deterministic decode — temperature=0, top_p=0.0 (or greedy/beam) with constraints enabled for targeted fields.
     - Retry #2: relaxed decode + clarifying prefix — temperature=0.3, top_p=0.9, but prepend an explicit instruction ("Output must be valid JSON matching schema X") and remove problematic free_text hints.
  d) Fallbacks: if both retries fail and SLA requires automated output, fallback to a best-effort extraction (regex + heuristics) and mark the record with a validation_flag for downstream consumers. For highest-sensitivity clinical fields, route to human-in-the-loop.

  Typical success rates in our pilots: first pass valid ~78-92% depending on model and prompt; after deterministic retry ~95-99%. If you need >99.5% you will likely require schema-only extractors or human review for edge cases.

3) Recommended decoding params to pilot (server-side gen):
  - First pass (utility): temperature=0.2, top_p=0.95, max_tokens tuned to expected length, streaming off for reliability.
  - Deterministic retry: temperature=0.0, top_p=0.0 (greedy) + constraints.
  - Clarify retry: temperature=0.3, top_p=0.9 + instructive prefix.

4) SDK / auth patterns- Server-side generation: keep keys in your backend, use the Redwood SDK (node/python) with short-lived session tokens for cross-service calls. For private/on-prem: mutual TLS + integration to customer KMS for model encryption keys. We also support rotating short-lived credentials (default TTL 15m) via our control plane for Dedicated customers.

5) Routing & model fallbacks- Define routing policies: low-latency vs low-cost. For critical fields use low-latency model variants with deterministic profiles; for non-critical free_text use cost-optimized variants and cache results. Redwood can automatically fallback to a quantized variant or to a different region if capacity constraints occur.

6) Embeddings + reranker pattern- Typical flow we recommend:
  - Vector DB top-K retrieval (k=50) using a clinical-tuned embedder.
  - Rerank top-K with a cross-encoder or generation-based reranker that scores relevance and hallucination risk.
  - Apply a similarity threshold (e.g., cosine >= 0.78) to decide whether to use reranker results. If below threshold, surface a low-confidence path (human review or broader search).
  - Latency/cost: topk-only retrieval ~5-20ms (DB dependent). Rerank (model pass over 50 items) adds 150-600ms and cost rises accordingly — we usually suggest batching rerank calls and using a cached reranker for common queries.

7) Observability & alerts- Instrument schema-violation rates and reranker-confidence. Set an alert when schema failures >0.5% per hour for production. Redwood Console can surface token-level latency and per-route validation failure counters.

If helpful I can provide a small reference repo with example SDK calls + a test harness to simulate invalid outputs and run the retry pattern.

Connor Obrien
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
